name: Oven drying at 103-105 C
description: Drying to constant mass at 103-105 C. The temperature matters - a lower-temperature or vacuum drying gives a different figure for the same material, which is exactly why the method is recorded beside the value and not inside the parameter

name: Oven drying at 60 C
description: Low-temperature drying, common where volatiles would be lost at 105 C

name: Ashing at 550 C
description: Incineration to constant mass at 550 C

name: Ashing at 600 C
description: Incineration to constant mass at 600 C

name: Ether extraction (diethyl ether)
description: Continuous or Soxhlet extraction with diethyl ether. This is what the Weende scheme calls crude fat - a method of determining total fat, not a different analyte

name: Ether extraction (petroleum ether)
description: Extraction with petroleum ether. Recovers a slightly different lipid set than diethyl ether

name: Acid hydrolysis then ether extraction
description: HCl hydrolysis before extraction, which releases bound lipids the plain ether extract leaves behind. Systematically higher than ee-diethyl on the same material

name: Acid detergent lignin (Van Soest)
description: Lignin as the residue of the acid-detergent sequence. feedtables.com defines its Lignin column as usually this method - note the hedge, which is why a value from a column headed only Lignin is recorded as method unknown rather than as this one

name: Klason lignin
description: Lignin as the residue after 72 percent sulphuric acid hydrolysis. Reads systematically higher than ADL

name: Permanganate lignin (Van Soest)
description: The permanganate variant of the Van Soest lignin determination

name: NDF with amylase (aNDF)
description: Neutral detergent fibre run with heat-stable amylase, so residual starch does not inflate the figure

name: NDF corrected for ash (aNDFom)
description: Neutral detergent fibre expressed free of residual ash

name: Starch by polarimetry (Ewers)
description: The polarimetric determination. Reads higher than the enzymatic method on the same material - Feedipedia prints both for several feeds

name: Starch by enzymatic assay
description: Enzymatic determination

name: Kjeldahl nitrogen
description: Wet digestion nitrogen determination

name: Dumas combustion nitrogen
description: Combustion nitrogen determination

name: Predicted from a regression equation
description: NOT A MEASUREMENT. The value is the output of an equation fitted to other constituents. Record it on value_origin as predicted - this method row exists for the case where the source names the equation

name: Ash deformation temperature, oxidising conditions
description: Ash melting determined in an oxidising atmosphere. The reducing-atmosphere value differs and is a separate determination of the same analyte

name: Ash deformation temperature, reducing conditions
description: Ash melting determined in a reducing atmosphere

name: Ash melting, American standard method
description: ASTM D1857-style cone test. Defines the four points IDT / ST / HT / FT. The ATMOSPHERE is recorded on the measurement notes, not here: oxidising and reducing conditions give different temperatures for the same cone and both are printed under this one standard

name: Ash melting, European standard method
description: CEN/TS 15370-style cone test. Defines SH / DEF / HE / FL. NOT the same point list as the American method: shrinkage (SH) has no American counterpart, and CEN reports no separate softening point

name: Cellulose and hemicellulose by difference from the detergent fractions
description: The van Soest sequence read as cellulose = ADF - ADL and hemicellulose = NDF - ADF. Phyllis2 prints `van Soest` against such a value. It is a DIFFERENT DETERMINATION from a sugar analysis of the same wall and it gives a different number

name: Cellulose and hemicellulose from monomeric sugar analysis
description: The wall hydrolysed and its monomer sugars quantified, then summed into cellulose and hemicellulose. Phyllis2 prints `Sugar Analysis`. On wheat bran it gives cellulose 13,80 wt% dry where van Soest gives 12,00 - the case that made this axis necessary

name: Extractives, ethanol/toluene
description: The classic wood-chemistry extraction

name: Extractives, 95% ethanol
description: A less exhaustive extraction than ethanol/toluene

name: Extractives, hot water
description: Water-soluble matter. Recovers a different set of compounds again, which is why the solvent is a method on one analyte and not three analytes
